_doc: Measurement PROFILE — FX majors. A reusable per-asset-class set of DEFAULTS for the surface fields of a sealed MC-* MeasurementContract instance. NOT a contract instance and NOT an admissibility seal. Charter: docs/governance/MEASUREMENT_CONTRACT.md section 9.

subordinate_to.relationship: Profiles supply reusable per-asset-class DEFAULTS that a sealed MC-* instance inherits. Every enumerated value below is drawn from the frozen schema's own enums so that subordination is mechanically checkable. A profile never overrides the charter, never relaxes the E0-E4 bar, and never sets trust_status. OVERRIDE PRECEDENCE (2026-08-06, engine_gate discussion): an MC-* instance ALWAYS WINS on any field the frozen schema scopes per-experiment rather than per-asset-class -- concretely pipeline_identity.engine_gate_mode, pipeline_identity.dataset_integrity_level, splits.*, and metrics.multiplicity/control-protocol. This profile's surface_defaults for those fields are non-binding suggestions only, retained for convenience; the sealed instance's own declared value is authoritative. This was made explicit after F-058 showed gate mode is pipeline IDENTITY (which object was measured), not an asset-class property -- a profile default must never be mistaken for that identity.

profile.rationale: Second asset class, added to test whether crypto-derived conclusions generalize. Needs its own profile primarily because of cost scale: a flat 12bps is 1.8-2.5x the median FX M15 bar, which makes any magnitude claim cost-dominated (F-035).

population.instruments_note: REQUIRES_DECISION. F-035 states '5 FX majors' but the always-loaded index does not name them; identities must be pinned from the F-035 corpus rather than guessed. XAUUSD is explicitly NOT in this profile — it REJECTs the FX holiday-gap gate and belongs to metals_mt5.

features.normalization_note: F-061/F-064: legacy equals corrected x close, so degeneracy is instrument-dependent. On FX (close near 1) the legacy basis binds differently than on crypto — a concrete reason this is a per-asset-class term.
features.session_note: REQUIRES_DECISION. F-066 proves MT5-sourced session/hour_of_day derive from broker-server time mislabelled UTC. The FEATURE was fixed config-gated; the live FILTER was deliberately left on broker time as a separate economic decision. A profile must say which basis its claims assume, because the two surfaces disagree by construction.

labels.note: Byte-identical to the crypto profile by design. This is the one surface that MUST NOT vary by asset class, or F-035's crypto-to-FX generalization claim becomes uninterpretable.

components.name: round_trip
components.bps_or_formula: DERIVED: k * median(bar_range_pct) computed per instrument from its own M15 corpus; k pending calibration

costs.legacy_note: F-035 records the concrete failure: at 12bps the cost is 1.8-2.5x the median FX M15 bar, so magnitude claims are cost-dominated. The direction of that null was argued robust because PF was far below 1, but magnitude was not recoverable. This is the strongest single argument for per-asset-class cost derivation.

metrics.provenance: Inherited from the historical M4 gate, UNVERIFIED. F-035 explicitly ran 'the VERBATIM M4 gate' at 2000 permutations.
